newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine bonds much lower as more sellers emerge.
newsitem.headline: Argentine bonds much lower as more sellers emerge.

text.p: Argentine bonds finished much lower Thursday as more sellers emerged as a result of the negative impact of U.S. Federal Reserve Chairman Alan Greenspan's statements a day earlier.
"We will continue with high volatility a couple of sessions more," said a trader at a local bank. "There was a lot of selling today."
Argentina's FRB due 2005 skidded 1-1/8 to 90-3/8, while the dollar-denominateed Bocon Previsional 2 due 2001 fell $0.70 to 125.90.
Peso bonds were the hardest hit, plummetting amid heavy trade. The peso-denominated Bocon Proveedor 1 due 2007 plunged 2.80 pesos to 103.00.
Another trader reported that hedge fund selling of Brady bonds abroad compounded the situation.
However, players overwhelmingly said the declines were welcome after the sharp run up in prices during January and February.
"I think its a healthy a correction - something that was necessary," said the second trader.
But he added: "I still think the only trend is up."
Operators pointed out that the strong economic fundamentals in Latin America and lack of bad news out of the region made it likely the sell-off would only last a couple of days more.
In the money markets, call money rates fell to 5.53 percent from 5.88 percent.
